short_description: Search, list, and read files from your Google Drive with version-aware content extraction.
store_description: Google's official hosted Drive MCP server (Workspace Developer Preview). IMPORTANT: This server requires manual setup before it can be used. (1) Join the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program at https://developers.google.com/workspace/preview. (2) In your Google Cloud project, enable BOTH APIs: 'drive.googleapis.com' (the REST API) and 'drivemcp.googleapis.com' (the MCP service). (3) Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application) at https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials with redirect URI 'http://127.0.0.1:3088/api/mcp/oauth/callback'. (4) In Google Auth Platform > Clients, open the OAuth client and check 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent'. This flag is MANDATORY from November 11, 2026 — Google will reject any OAuth client without it. (5) Set PELDRUN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and PELDRUN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables. (6) Add your Google account as a test user on the OAuth consent screen. Once configured, the server exposes read-only Drive tools by default: drive_search_files, drive_read_file_content (Docs as markdown, Sheets as CSV, Slides as text), drive_list_files, drive_get_file_metadata. Adding 'drive.file' to the scopes list enables file creation and editing tools.
description: Official Google Drive MCP server — search and read Drive files.
usage_hint: Drive MCP exposes read-only tools by default. WORKFLOW: (1) When the user names a file but you do not have an ID, call drive_search_files with name and/or MIME type filters (Google Docs: 'application/vnd.google-apps.document', Sheets: 'application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet', Slides: 'application/vnd.google-apps.presentation'). (2) Call drive_read_file_content with the returned fileId — Docs return markdown, Sheets return CSV, Slides return text. (3) Use drive_list_files to browse a folder by parentId. (4) Use drive_get_file_metadata when the user asks about sharing permissions or file size. Adding the 'drive.file' scope enables write tools. Note: drive.file only grants access to files the app creates or that the user explicitly opens with the app; drive.readonly is required for searching across the whole Drive.
